 :: J U D G M E N T :
:
Petitioners have filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the death of deceased N. Narayanaswamy in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 16.01.2022, one Sri. N. Narayanaswamy was proceeding by riding the Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA03JS 3638 towards Handiganala village from Siddlaghatta.
At about 3.00 p.m., near KSRTC Bus Stand infront of Police Chowki, the deceased was entering into SidlaghattaChikkaballapura main road carefully and cautiously by ensuring no vehicle near to him.

At that time one light goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA07A 3556 driven by its driver from Chikkaballapura side in a rash or negligent manner with high speed, due to which he lost control over the vehicle and went to wrong side of the road and dashed against the scooter.
As a result, Sri.
Narayanaswamy fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital, Sidlaghatta.

After first aid, he was shifted to Baptist Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein Sri. Narayanaswamy undergone surgery of decompressive Craniectomy.
Though, in spite of better treatment, Narayanaswamy succumbed to injuries on 18.01.2022 at about 2.51 p.m.

Thereafter, the dead body of the deceased Narayanaswamy was shifted to General hospital,
Sidlaghatta, wherein postmortem was conducted.
The deceased was aged about 65 years at the time of death.

He was earning more than Rs.50,000/
per month by doing coconut business in the shop situated at Sidlaghatta.
The petitioners have no other source of income, hence they are entirely depending on the earnings of deceased.
Due to death of deceased, the petitioners are put to lot of mental agony and untold misery.
The petitioners have spent Rs.5,00,000/ towards treatment of deceased, transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.

The accident in question was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of Goods Vehicle bearing Munirathnamma vs N. Prakash on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114869425/
2 Reg.No.KA07A3556 by its driver.
The 1st respondent is the RC owner of aforesaid goods vehicle and the 2 nd respondent is the insurer.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
With these averments petitioners prays to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the 1st respondent remained absent and he was placed Exparte.
The 2nd respondents appeared through its counsels and filed written statement.
4. The 2nd respondent/Insurance company has contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
The 2nd respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy and its validity with respect to offending vehicle.
However, contended that, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Interalia contended that, without knowledge of riding and without wearing helmet, the deceased was riding the Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA03 JS 3638 in a rash or negligent manner with high speed and caused the accident.
Hence, the deceased sustained injuries due to self accident and the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident.

It is contended that, if it is proved that, the insured vehicle was involved in the accident,
drivers of both the vehicles are responsible for the alleged accident.
Thus, the liability is reduced to the extent of negligence of the deceased.
This respondent has denied the amount spent by the petitioners, occupation and income of deceased.
It is further contended that, driver of the offending vehicle has not possessed valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle.

Further contended that, the 1st respondent has not complied the mandatory provision of Sec.134 (c), 158(6) of M.V.
Act.
The claim made by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
With these averments, this respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following:
:ISSUES:

1.Whether petitioners prove that N. Narayanaswamy was died on 18.01.2022 due to the injuries sustained in the accident caused on 16.01.2022 by rider of motor cycle bearing Registration No.KA 03JS3638 as stated in the petition?

2.Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?
3.Whether the petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for?
4.What order or award?
6.
It is relevant to note that, as on the date of accident, the deceased was going on Honda Activa scooter bearing Reg.No.KA03JS3638 and offending vehicle is bearing Reg.No.KA07A3556.
Therefore, Issue No.1 has to be recast.

Accordingly Issue No.1 is recast as hereunder:
1.

Whether petitioners prove that N. Narayanaswamy was died on 18.01.2022 owing to injuries sustained in the accident caused on 16.01.2022 due to rash or negligent driving of Light Goods vehicle bearing Registration No.KA07 A3556 by its driver Munirathnamma vs N. Prakash on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114869425/
3 as stated in the petition?
7. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.1 was examined as PW.1 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.
Learned counsel for Respondent No.2 has crossexamined P.W.1.
Respondents have not adduced any evidence.
8. Heard the arguments of both side.
Perused the materials placed on record.

The findings of the Tribunal to the above referred issues are as under:
 Recast Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3 : In the Partly Affirmative.
 Issue No.4 : As per the final order for  the following:
 :REASONS:
 9.
Recast
ISSUE Nos.1 and 2: These two issues are inter connected.
Hence, they have taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition.

10. The case of the petitioners is that, one N. Narayanaswamy was died on 18.01.2022 at about 2.50 p.m., while taking treatment for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident occurred on 16.01.2022 at about 3.00 p.m., near KSRTC Bus Stand, infront of Police Chowki on Sidlaghat6ta Chikkaballapura main road, due to rash or negligent driving of goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA 07A3665 by its driver.
Further case of the petitioners is that, the deceased was a Coconut merchant having shop at Sidlaghatta town and he was earning more than Rs.50,000/ per month.
The petitioners have no any other source of income, hence, they were depending on the deceased.
It is the case of the petitioners that, the Sidlaghatta Town police have also registered the case against the driver of offending vehicle.
11. In order to prove the claim of petitioners, the petitioner No.1 was examined as P.W.1 by filing affidavit.
P.W.1 also produced as many as 19 documents, which have been marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.
Ex.P.Series Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR pertaining to Cr.No.8/2022.
Ex. P.2
is the true copy of complaint.

Ex . P.14

Ex.P.19 are the medical bills.

12. According to the respondent No.2, the accident was not occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of light Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA07A3556 by its driver, percontra the accident occurred due to the negligence of deceased, who has no knowledge of riding the scooter and without wearing helmet.
Though the policy was in force, liability of the 2 nd respondent is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
2 nd respondent also disputed the age and income of the deceased.
13. Before going to discuss the issues, it is appropriate to say the admitted facts of the case.
There is no dispute with regard to death of N. Narayanaswamy in the road traffic accident.
The respondents have not seriously disputed the relationship of petitioners with deceased N. Narayanaswamy.
14. So, now the important question before this Tribunal is to find whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle or not?
In order to answer this aspect, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.
On careful perusal of these documents, it is clear that, criminal case was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Apart from that, charge sheet was submitted against the driver of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P.13.

It is relevant to note that,
though the respondent No.2 has contended that, accident was occurred due to the negligence of the deceased, however, in order to substantiate the same, the 2nd respondent has not placed any material before this Tribunal.

Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
15. Now, the next aspect is with regard to age and income of the deceased.
In the instant case, the respondent No.2 has disputed the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 65 years.
P.W.1 was also deposed that, her husband was aged about 65 years at the time of his death.
In order to substantiate the same, she has produced the election I.D. Card of deceased N. Narayanaswamy, which is marked as Ex.P.16.
On careful perusal of this document, it reveals that, the age of the deceased was 39 years as on 01.01.2002.

However,
P.W.1 herself has stated the age of deceased as 65 years.
Therefore, age of the deceased is considered as 65 years at the time of accident.
16. Now, the next aspect is with respect to income of deceased.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was having shop at Sidlaghatta and by doing coconut business he was earning Rs.50,000/ per month.
However, to substantiate the exact income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MVI) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
Munirathnamma vs N. Prakash on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114869425/
5 "
In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/ per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".
17. In the instant case also, the petitioners have not produced the documents to establish the income of deceased.

As such in the absence of authentic document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/ per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 16.01.2022.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,500/ per month.
Accordingly, Recasted Issue No.1 and 2 are answered in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE No.3:
This issue is with regard to entitlement of relief.
According to the petition averments, petitioner No.1 is the wife of deceased, petitioner No.2 is the son of deceased.
The 1 st petitioner has lost her husband and 2nd petitioner has lost her loving father.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.

At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered in M.F.A.No.102868 of 2014 (M.V.D.), between Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court held that, "even if the dependency is relevant criteria to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency and the dependency includes gratuitous service dependency,
physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency so on and so forth,
which can never be equated in terms of the money.

entities.text: Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even married sons and daughters are entitled for compensation not only on conventional heads, but also on loss of dependency".
Hence, Petitioners No.1 and 2 are considered as dependents of deceased.

19. Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioners have established the age of deceased i.e.,
as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 65 years.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident,
the income with respect to the future prospect has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is relevant to note that The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for the age of the deceased and percentage of future prospects as hereunder:
"If the deceased is self employed or fixed salary, his age below 40 years, future prospects is 40%".
"If the deceased between 40 to 50 years age, future prospects is 25%".

"If the deceased between 50 to 60 years age, future prospects is 10% and if the deceased more than 60 years, no addition as future prospects".
Munirathnamma vs N. Prakash on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114869425/
6 20.
Admittedly, the deceased is not a permanent job holder and he is not a fixed salary person.
The deceased was aged about 65 years and therefore, no additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
So, monthly income of deceased is taken at Rs.15,500/, which would meet the ends of justice.
21. The 1st petitioner is the wife and 2nd petitioner is the son of deceased.
Already this court has observed that, petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are the dependents of the deceased.
Therefore, by applying the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma case, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.
The same comes to Rs.15,500 - 5,166/ =Rs.10,334/.

Then total income of the deceased per annum comes to Rs.1,24,008/
(Rs.10,334 x 12 = 1,24,008/)
22. The deceased was 65 years old at the time of death, the multiplier 7 is applied, which is appropriate to the age of deceased.

Then the loss of dependency is calculated as hereunder:
Rs.1,24,008/ X 7 = Rs.8,68,056/.
Therefore, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.8,68,056/ under the head of loss of dependency.
23. P.W.1 in his affidavit has stated that, after the accident, her husband was shifted to Government Hospital, Sidlaghatta.
After first he was shifted to Bangalore Baptist Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein her husband undergone surgery.
Despite of best treatment, her husband succumbed to injuries on 18.01.2022.

Further, P.W.1 deposed that, they have spent Rs.5,00,000/ towards treatment,
conveyance, transportation of dead body and funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
To substantiate her contention, P.W.1 has produced Ex.P.19 16 Medical Bills for Rs.2,14,518/.
Ex.P.19 includes final bill.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that, certain bill amount has been refunded under Scheme 20.
Therefore, the petitioners are not entitled for those bill amount.

Apart from that,
during the course of crossexamination of P.W.1, learned counsel for respondent No.2 suggested that, medical bills were created.
Further P.W.1 deposed that, she can examine the person who issued the medical bills.
Now it is appropriate to see bills at Sr.No.2 to Sr.No.16.
On perusal of these bills, it appears to this Tribunal that, Sr.No.2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10 to 16, customer name is mentioned as friend of Baptist and Sr.No.3, 6, 8 customer name is mentioned as Scheme 20.
It is relevant to note that, respondent No.2 has disputed only with respect to bills issued under Scheme 20.
However, he has not disputed other bills.
It is relevant to note that, the respondent has not explained Scheme 20 appeared in Sr.No.3, Sr.No.6, Sr.No.8.
Apart from that, there are no documents forthcoming from the side of respondent No.2 regarding those bills were reimbursed.

24. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners have contended that, they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
In order to substantiate the same, they have not produced any documents.

Now the question before this Tribunal is whether petitioners No.2 is also Munirathnamma vs N. Prakash on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114869425/
7
entitled for consortium or not?
Admittedly, the 1st petitioner is the wife and she is entitled for spousal consortium.
Admittedly the petitioner No.2 is the son of deceased.
At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2018 (1) SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the parents and children are having right to get the compensation under filial consortium.
Therefore, the 1st petitioner is entitled for Rs.40,000/ under the head of spousal consortium and petitioners No.2 is entitled for Rs.40,000/ under the head of filial consortium.
Further, Rs.15,000/ is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.15,000/ is awarded towards loss of estate.

25. The details of compensation amount is as under:
 S.No. Heads Rs.

1 . Towards loss of Rs. 8,68,056/
 Dependency spousal  and filial consortium,
 2. Towards spousal and Rs. 80,000/
 40,000 X 2  filial consortium,
 3. Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/
 4. Funeral expense Rs. 15,000/
 5. Towards Medical Rs. 2,14,518/
 expenses.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.11,92,574/
26.
Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:
Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Hence, it is held that, the driver of offending vehicle was holding valid and effective D.L. as on the date of alleged accident.
Insurance Policy and liability:
Respondent No.2 the insurance company has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending vehicle.
Hence, it is held that, insurance coverage of the vehicle was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, the respondent No.2 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioners.
Interest:

In view of the decision reported in MFA NO:
301312019 dtd, 12.5.2020, rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
Accordingly, this Tribunal is answered Issue No. 3 in Partly Affirmative.
27. ISSUE No.4:. In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following.

Munirathnamma vs N. Prakash on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114869425/
8 :ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.

Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.11,92,574/ (Rupees Eleven Lakhs,
Ninety Two Thousand Five Hundred and Seventy Four Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.
 Respondent No.2 being insurer of the  offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and directed to deposit the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
:
APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :

On deposit of compensation amount,
 Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 75% and petitioner No.2 is entitled for 25% with interest.

50% of share of petitioner No.1 with interest is to be paid to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of Epayment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 50% of her share with interest shall be invested in F.D. in her name in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years.
It is clarified that, the 1 st petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
Entire share of petitioner No.2 with interest is to be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E payment on proper identification as per rules.

Act.
The claim made by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.

2.Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?
3.Whether the petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for?
4.What order or award?

14. So, now the important question before this Tribunal is to find whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle or not?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
In the instant case, the respondent No.2 has disputed the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Therefore, age of the deceased is considered as 65 years at the time of accident.
However, to substantiate the exact income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
17. In the instant case also, the petitioners have not produced the documents to establish the income of deceased.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,500/ per month.
The 1 st petitioner has lost her husband and 2nd petitioner has lost her loving father.
At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered in M.F.A.No.102868 of 2014 (M.V.D.), between Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court held that, "even if the dependency is relevant criteria to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency and the dependency includes gratuitous service dependency,
physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency so on and so forth,
which can never be equated in terms of the money.
Hence, Petitioners No.1 and 2 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Admittedly, the deceased is not a permanent job holder and he is not a fixed salary person.
The deceased was aged about 65 years and therefore, no additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
So, monthly income of deceased is taken at Rs.15,500/, which would meet the ends of justice.
21. The 1st petitioner is the wife and 2nd petitioner is the son of deceased.
Therefore, by applying the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma case, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.
24. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.

Further, Rs.15,000/ is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.15,000/ is awarded towards loss of estate.
